research_question: Can the five retained DE/RU gaps, the speaker structure of all selected core-reading evidence, and five competing interpretation axes be prepared for bounded source-visible review without correcting witnesses, accepting alignments, impersonating human review, or promoting semantic authority?

scope.speaker_population: every parent core/supporting evidence unit in the four declared core readings

method.source_return: reconstruct exact frozen DE/RU alignment slices and the one related Russian verse row; verify tracked digests before analysis
method.gap_policy: preserve observed text privately; publish only digests, addresses, mechanical explanations, and reversible proposals
method.speaker_policy: attribute discourse roles from source-order transitions and explicit reporting cues; retain mixed and performative-voice alternatives
method.interpretation_policy: bind each axis to positive evidence, counterpressure, speaker dependencies, and falsifying review questions
method.review_compression: prepare all 159 speaker candidates but route only ambiguous boundaries, five gaps, and interpretation axes to the exception worklist

risk: medium: source-order speaker inference and interpretive evidence selection can be mistaken for accepted authorship or doctrine; explicit alternatives, counterpressure, unreviewed status, private exact text, and zero semantic/graph/canon effect constrain the risk
rollback: remove only this review-preparation subroute, its ignored private analysis, its builder, focused test, and additive inventory entries; do not alter witnesses, technical markup, alignments, parent candidate, review ledger, canon, graph, or exports
authority_boundary: agent-generated review preparation only; no witness correction, accepted alignment, human review, accepted speaker attribution, sign, concept, claim, relation, graph fact, or canon effect
